subjects.subject: angular
subjects.summary: Angular terms, from first components to server-side rendering.
subjects.blurb: Read a definition, then pick the matching term. Four levels, from Beginner to Mastery.

decks.title: Beginner
decks.description: Components, templates, binding, directives, services, and routing. {count} terms.

decks.title: Intermediate
decks.description: Change detection, lifecycle hooks, forms, HTTP, and component communication. {count} terms.

decks.description: Signals, standalone components, dependency injection, guards, and lazy loading. {count} terms.

decks.title: Mastery
decks.description: Server-side rendering, hydration, performance, and app architecture. {count} terms.

cards.Component: A class, template, and styles that control a view.
cards.Module (NgModule): A container that organizes related components, directives, and pipes.
cards.Template: HTML markup that defines a component’s view.
cards.Metadata: Configuration attached to classes using decorators.
cards.Decorator: A TypeScript feature used to attach metadata to classes.
cards.Data Binding: A way to connect component data with the template.
cards.Interpolation: A one-way binding that displays data using {{ }}.
cards.Property Binding: A one-way binding that sets element or component properties.
cards.Event Binding: A one-way binding that listens for events from elements.
cards.Two-Way Binding: A binding that updates both the view and the component.
cards.Directive: A class that adds behavior to elements.
cards.Structural Directive: A directive that changes layout by adding or removing elements.
cards.Attribute Directive: A directive that changes the appearance or behavior of an element.
cards.Pipe: A class that transforms displayed data in templates.
cards.Service: A class that provides reusable logic or data.
cards.Dependency Injection: A system that supplies classes with needed services.
cards.Routing: A system that maps URLs to components.
cards.Router Module: A module that configures and manages routes.
cards.RxJS: A library that provides Observables and operators.
cards.Environment Files: Files that store configuration values for different builds.
cards.Assets: Static files such as images or JSON served with the application.
cards.Global Styles: Stylesheets applied across the entire application.
cards.RouterLinkActive: A directive that marks active navigation links.

cards.Change Detection: A process that updates the view when data changes.
cards.Zone.js: A library that helps Angular detect asynchronous operations.
cards.Lifecycle Hooks: Methods that run at specific times in a component’s life.
cards.ngOnInit: A lifecycle hook that runs after component initialization.
cards.ngOnDestroy: A lifecycle hook that runs just before a component is removed.
cards.FormsModule: A module that supports template-driven forms.
cards.ReactiveFormsModule: A module that supports reactive forms.
cards.FormControl: An object that tracks a single form input’s value and state.
cards.FormGroup: An object that groups multiple FormControls.
cards.Validators: Functions that check form input rules.
cards.HttpClient: A service for making HTTP requests.
cards.HttpInterceptor: A class that modifies HTTP requests or responses.
cards.Input Binding: A way to pass data from a parent component to a child.
cards.Output Binding: A way for a child component to send events to a parent.
cards.Content Projection: A way to insert external content into a component’s template.
cards.ViewChild: A way to access a single element or component in the view.
cards.ViewChildren: A way to access multiple elements or components in the view.
cards.TemplateRef: A reference to an embedded template.
cards.ChangeDetectorRef: A service that lets you control change detection manually.
cards.Angular CLI: A tool for generating, building, and managing Angular projects.
cards.Route Parameters: Values passed through the URL to load specific data.
cards.Query Parameters: Extra values added to a URL for filtering or state.
cards.ActivatedRoute: An object that provides information about the current route.
cards.HttpHeaders: An object that sets metadata on HTTP requests.
cards.HttpParams: An object that builds query parameters for HTTP requests.
cards.Async Pipe: A pipe that subscribes to Observables and displays their values.
cards.TrackBy Function: A function that improves rendering performance in lists.

cards.Standalone Component: A component that does not require a module.
cards.Signal: A value that notifies Angular when it changes.
cards.Computed Signal: A value derived from one or more signals.
cards.Effect: A function that runs when signals change.
cards.Injector Tree: A structure that determines where services are created.
cards.Hierarchical DI: A dependency injection pattern based on nested injectors.
cards.AOT Compilation: A build step that converts templates into optimized code.
cards.Ivy: Angular’s rendering engine that improves build and runtime performance.
cards.View Engine: Angular’s older rendering engine replaced by Ivy.
cards.Dynamic Component Loading: Creating components at runtime using Angular APIs.
cards.Renderer2: An API for safely manipulating the DOM.
cards.HostListener: A decorator that listens to events on the host element.
cards.HostBinding: A decorator that binds properties to the host element.
cards.Custom Pipe: A user-defined class that transforms data in templates.
cards.Custom Directive: A user-defined class that adds behavior to elements.
cards.Route Guard: A class that controls navigation decisions.
cards.Resolver: A class that loads data before a route activates.
cards.Lazy Loading: Loading components or modules only when needed.
cards.Preloading Strategy: A rule that determines how lazy-loaded modules are prefetched.
cards.NgRx: A library for managing global state using actions and reducers.
cards.Functional Guard: A route guard written as a function instead of a class.
cards.Functional Interceptor: An HTTP interceptor written as a function.
cards.Template Variables: Variables declared inside templates for cleaner logic.
cards.Signals-based Inputs: Inputs that use signals instead of bindings.
cards.DestroyRef: A reference used to register cleanup logic.
cards.provideHttpClient: A function that configures HTTP services for an application.
cards.provideRouter: A function that configures routing for an application.

cards.Server-Side Rendering: Rendering pages on the server to improve load time and visibility.
cards.Hydration: Reusing server-rendered HTML on the client to avoid re-rendering.
cards.Angular Universal: Tools that enable server-side rendering and hydration.
cards.Zone-less Mode: Running Angular without Zone.js for improved performance.
cards.Event Replay: A hydration feature that replays user events after startup.
cards.Deferred Loading: Loading components only when they become visible or needed.
cards.View Transitions: Smooth page transitions supported by Angular.
cards.Signals-based Forms: Forms built using signals instead of form controls.
cards.Build Optimizations: Techniques that reduce bundle size and improve performance.
cards.Bundle Budgeting: Limits that prevent bundle size from growing too large.
cards.Standalone Architecture: Application structure built entirely without modules.
cards.Feature Shell Architecture: A pattern that organizes large apps into isolated areas.
cards.Custom Hydration Strategies: Advanced ways to tune hydration behavior.
cards.Signals-based State Architecture: Application state managed entirely with signals.
cards.ComponentStore: A lightweight state management pattern for components.
cards.Performance Profiling: Analyzing rendering and change detection behavior.
cards.SSR Caching: Storing server-rendered pages for faster responses.
cards.Edge Rendering: Running server-side rendering close to users for speed.

cards.Cloud Computing: Delivery of computing services over the internet.
cards.Public Cloud: Cloud resources owned and operated by a third-party provider.
cards.Private Cloud: Cloud resources used exclusively by one organization.
cards.Hybrid Cloud: A mix of public and private cloud environments.
cards.IaaS: Cloud model that provides virtual machines and storage.
cards.PaaS: Cloud model that provides managed application hosting and tools.
cards.SaaS: Cloud model that delivers fully managed applications.
cards.Scalability: Ability to increase or decrease resources as needed.
cards.Elasticity: Automatic scaling of resources based on demand.
cards.High Availability: Ensuring services remain accessible with minimal downtime.
cards.Azure Portal: A web-based interface for managing Azure resources.
cards.Azure Resource Manager: A system that deploys and manages Azure resources.
cards.Resource Group: A container that holds related Azure resources.
cards.Subscription: A billing and access boundary for Azure resources.
cards.Management Group: A container for organizing multiple subscriptions.
cards.Region: A geographic area containing Azure datacenters.
cards.Availability Zone: Physically separate datacenters within a region.
cards.Virtual Machine: An on-demand computing resource running in Azure.
cards.Virtual Network: A private network for Azure resources.
cards.Subnet: A segment of a virtual network.
cards.Network Security Group: A set of rules that control network traffic.
cards.Azure Storage Account: A container for storing data objects in Azure.
cards.File Storage: Managed file shares accessible over SMB.
cards.Azure Cosmos DB: A globally distributed NoSQL database service.
cards.Azure Functions: A serverless compute service that runs event-driven code.
cards.App Service: A platform for hosting web apps and APIs.
cards.Azure Active Directory: A cloud identity and access management service.
cards.Multi-Factor Authentication: A security method requiring multiple verification steps.
cards.Role-Based Access Control: A system that assigns permissions based on roles.
cards.Azure Policy: A service that enforces rules across Azure resources.
cards.Azure Blueprints: A tool for deploying governed environments.
cards.Cost Management: Tools for tracking and optimizing cloud spending.
cards.Azure Advisor: A service that provides recommendations for optimization.
cards.Service Level Agreement: A contract that defines uptime and performance guarantees.
cards.Shared Responsibility Model: A framework defining security roles between provider and customer.
